items.title: VRU-Accident: A Vision-Language Benchmark for Video Question Answering and Dense Captioning for Accident Scene Understanding
items.raw_content:
Authors: Younggun Kim, Ahmed S. Abdelrahman, Mohamed Abdel-Aty

Ensuring the safety of vulnerable road users (VRUs), such as pedestrians and cyclists, is a critical challenge for autonomous driving systems, as crashes involving VRUs often result in severe or fatal consequences. While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown promise in enhancing scene understanding and decision making in autonomous vehicles, there is currently no standardized benchmark to quantitatively evaluate their reasoning abilities in complex, safety-critical scenarios involving VRUs. To address this gap, we present VRU-Accident, a large-scale vision-language benchmark designed to evaluate MLLMs in high-risk traffic scenarios involving VRUs. VRU-Accident comprises 1K real-world dashcam accident videos, annotated with 6K multiple-choice question-answer pairs across six safety-critical categories (with 24K candidate options and 3.4K unique answer choices), as well as 1K dense scene descriptions. Unlike prior works, our benchmark focuses explicitly on VRU-vehicle accidents, providing rich, fine-grained annotations that capture both spatial-temporal dynamics and causal semantics of accidents. To assess the current landscape of MLLMs, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 state-of-the-art models on the multiple-choice VQA task and on the dense captioning task. Our findings reveal that while MLLMs perform reasonably well on visually grounded attributes, they face significant challenges in reasoning and describing accident causes, types, and preventability.

items.title: HNOSeg-XS: Extremely Small Hartley Neural Operator for Efficient and Resolution-Robust 3D Image Segmentation
items.title_zh: HNOSeg-XS：用于高效且分辨率鲁棒的 3D 图像分割的超小 Hartley 神经算子
items.summary: The paper proposes HNOSeg-XS, a resolution-robust 3D medical image segmentation architecture that models segmentation as learnable partial differential equations through a neural operator, replacing the Fourier transform with the Hartley transform. On BraTS'23, KiTS'23 and MVSeg'23 with a Tesla V100 GPU it used fewer than 34.7k parameters and posted the best inference time (under 0.24 s) and memory use (under 1.8 GiB) among the tested CNN and transformer models.

items.title: Compute Requirements for Algorithmic Innovation in Frontier AI Models

items.summary: The authors apply a dynamic embedded topic model to UNFCCC policy decisions from 1995 to 2023, excluding 2020, finding a shift from early emphasis on greenhouse gases and international conventions toward implementation, technical collaboration, capacity building, finance and global agreements.

items.title: Contrastive Conditional-Unconditional Alignment for Long-tailed Diffusion Model
items.title_zh: 面向长尾扩散模型的对比式条件—无条件对齐
items.summary: The paper proposes contrastive conditional-unconditional alignment (CCUA), combining an alignment loss with an unsupervised contrastive loss to improve the diversity and fidelity of tail-class images in class-conditional diffusion models trained on long-tailed data. The method is demonstrated on U-Net and Diffusion Transformer architectures and tested on datasets including ImageNet-LT at 256x256 resolution.

items.title: Leveraging Manifold Embeddings for Enhanced Graph Transformer Representations and Learning
items.title_zh: 利用流形嵌入增强图 Transformer 表示与学习
items.summary: Researchers prepend a lightweight Riemannian mixture-of-experts layer that routes each graph node to spherical, flat or hyperbolic manifolds, lifting accuracy by up to 3% on four node-classification benchmarks when inserted into an ensemble graph transformer.
